inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~826M = 823M basic on the Q2 FY2027 10-Q cover (2026-08-20) plus ~3M dilutive securities (Q1 FY27 diluted-basic spread 871-868). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution too would double-count. The FY2026 956M diluted count is stale: the Q1 FY2027 ~$27.2B debt-funded repurchase retired ~130M shares.
inputs.cash_note: Cash & equivalents 8,310 + current marketable securities 3,093 at 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q, SEC XBRL).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: CRM is net-DEBT (~$27.9B) after the Q1 FY27 leveraged buyback, so there is no net-cash pile being double-counted. FY2026 interest income was $539M.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation 3,509 + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 351 (SEC XBRL companyfacts). Salesforce publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1 FY2027: 1,763 + 327 = 9.3% of revenue, same as FY2026.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 repurchases $12.6B; H1 FY2027 $27.3B (of which $27.2B in Q1, debt-funded: total debt 14.4B -> 39.3B, equity 59.1B -> 34.2B). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded, and buybacks are value-neutral in this model (the cash is charged as SBC and the debt sits in net debt).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Rf ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (~3.9% after tax); D/V ~13% at market (net debt 27.9B vs ~193B market cap) -> WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside operating expense and hence inside EBITDA/the flows; lease liabilities (2,455 at 2026-07-31) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1: operating SaaS company; US filer, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md not required). First valuation of CRM. Base revenue is FY2026 (ended 2026-01-31) at 41,525; year 1 is FY2027 and is anchored to the Q2 FY27 raised guide of $46.1-46.4B. Adj. EBITDA = GAAP EBITDA + SBC (FY2026: 11,962 + 3,509 = 15,471, 37.3%), consistent with FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance of 34.3% plus ~3% depreciation. D&A line (3,631 in FY2026, 8.7%) excludes amortisation of capitalised commissions (2,197), whose net cash effect sits in working capital with deferred revenue; D&A is largely acquired-intangible amortisation (Slack, Tableau, MuleSoft, Informatica) and is glided down toward capex so the model does not perpetuate an amortisation tax shield. Pending acquisitions (Contentful, Fin) are included in management's FY27 revenue guide but their purchase consideration is undisclosed in the data here and NOT deducted; year-1 growth is set at the low-middle of the guide to limit that mismatch.

equity_bridge.item: Strategic investments (incl. Anthropic stake) at 75% of book
equity_bridge.note: OtherLongTermInvestments 11,324 at 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY27 10-Q XBRL), up from 7,772 at 2026-04-30 largely on the Anthropic mark. Gains on these sit below operating income and are excluded from the EBITDA flows, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). 25% haircut for private-company marks, illiquidity and tax on realisation.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.4% 3y / 7.3% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS: book value is driven by buybacks ($40B+ since FY2023, $27B in Q1 FY27 alone, cutting equity to 38.4B) and the 2021 Slack stock deal, not by the business. EPS 3y CAGR is meaningless off the restructuring-depressed FY2023 base (0.21 -> 7.85). Revenue 3y CAGR (9.8%, with ~1pt of Informatica in FY26) is used as the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC fell from ~10.5% of revenue (FY2023) to ~9.3% (FY2026) while margins expanded after the FY2023 restructuring; the owner-FCF series starts from a depressed FY2023 base, so its CAGR is not a forward guide. Equity-award withholding taxes are only captured from FY2026 (351); earlier years' owner FCF is overstated by that amount. Owner FCF: FY2021 1,901; FY2023 3,034; FY2024 6,711; FY2025 9,251; FY2026 10,542.

base.narrative: FY27 at the low-middle of the raised $46.1-46.4B guide (~3pts Informatica), then organic growth of 8-9% as Agentforce/Data 360 consumption offsets seat saturation, fading to 3.5%. Adj. EBITDA margin creeps from 37% to 40% (non-GAAP op margin ~37%); SBC glides 9.2% -> 7.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: Salesforce holds its ~20% CRM share and converts the agentic shift into consumption revenue: Agentforce + Data 360 ARR (~$3.9B, +210%) grows into a meaningful slice of revenue, roughly offsetting slower seat expansion in Sales and Service Cloud, so organic growth settles at 8-9% before fading. Informatica integrates on schedule and the FY27 34.3% non-GAAP margin inches up on internal AI productivity, partly eaten by token/inference costs (Anthropic spend). SBC declines slowly as a share of revenue; the leveraged buyback is financed, not repeated.
scenario_narratives.bull: Salesforce becomes the model-agnostic orchestration layer the Claudeforce partnership pitches: Data 360 + Informatica make it the trusted system of record agents run on, outcome/consumption pricing expands the TAM beyond seats, and growth re-accelerates to ~10-11% for several years. AI-driven internal productivity carries adj. EBITDA margin to 43% and lets SBC fall to ~6.5% of revenue. Requires Agentforce monetisation AND margin discipline AND no share loss to Microsoft - several things at once, hence the 25% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 'SaaSpocalypse' partly lands: AI agents from Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI and Anthropic-powered startups compress seat counts and per-seat pricing, HubSpot keeps taking the mid-market, and Agentforce revenue cannibalises rather than adds. Organic growth drops to 3-5% after the Informatica lap, rising inference costs and price concessions pull adj. EBITDA margin to 35%, and SBC stays ~8.5-9% because talent retention in an AI market is expensive. A structurally slower business earns a 14x exit cap and 2% perpetual growth; the $39B debt load raises the equity's sensitivity to this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because AI disintermediation of seat-based CRM is a live, unresolved structural risk (the stock fell 30-37% on it in H1 2026) and equity is now levered (~$27.9B net debt after the Q1 FY27 buyback). Base 50% as the guided, consensus-like path with contracted cRPO +14% support. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs Agentforce monetisation, margin expansion and share defence to all succeed together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Salesforce is valued as a mature, highly cash-generative SaaS franchise on an owner-FCF basis: SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes (~9.3% of revenue) is charged as a real cost, the share count is held flat, and the Q1 FY27 debt-funded buyback is reflected once, through the new share count and the higher net debt. Acquired-intangible amortisation is glided down toward capex so its tax shield is not capitalised in perpetuity, and the Anthropic-inclusive strategic investment book is added to equity at a 25% haircut.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI agents disintermediating seat-based CRM licensing (bear-case axis)
Leverage: $39.3B gross debt; a 1pp change in organic growth now moves equity value more than before the buyback
Pending Contentful and Fin acquisitions: purchase consideration not yet in net debt
Strategic-investment marks (Anthropic) are private and could reverse
Inference/token cost inflation compressing gross margin if agent pricing does not scale with usage
SBC staying near 9% of revenue rather than gliding down
